title: A unique prime over p plus going up (or down) pins down the localisation at p
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if there is a unique prime of S over p and either going up holds, or going down holds with at most one prime over every prime of R, then the localisation of S at p equals the localisation at that prime (statement lines 10013-10029). The proof does not argue with the fibres directly: it describes the primes of the localisation as those contracting below p, draws the resulting cube of primes, and uses going up or going down in the two branches to force any such prime to be the distinguished one, so that all elements outside it become invertible (proof lines 10031-10062). Reading the two hypotheses as two ways of closing the same cube is the content. H2.
